title: Companion Concierge micro-PRD (scratch)
content:
Context and motivation:

Quick brain-dump: customers (SMB apps + AI-native assistants) repeatedly ask for a lightweight, guided onboarding layer that stitches together Redwood's session / routing / cost controls + simple persona templates. The goal is not a full assistant product but a minimal ‘concierge’ surface that helps first-run users get value quickly and safely while we collect the right signals for longer-term personalization and routing choices.

Why this?
- Drop-off on first 3 sessions is high for new API users; many give up before they tune models/rollouts.
- Teams want a non-invasive experience that demonstrates low-latency, sane token-economics, and predictable quality without diving into SDK knobs.

This doc = micro-PRD + user stories + quick experiment plan. Rough, noisy, intentionally short.

Target scope (MVP):
- Small guided flow that runs in-hosted mode (no Dedicated / Private initially).
- 3-step onboarding: (1) choose intent + persona template, (2) sample prompt + fidelity slider, (3) test query + suggested routing (cost vs. quality).
- Under the hood: use existing API routes + a default model bundle (e.g., redwood/gpt-small-qual / redwood/gpt-small-econ variants) + prefix caching for the persona.
- Telemetry: capture session_id, selected persona, fidelity setting, first 10 queries, and per-query latency & token usage.

User stories (priority order):
1) As a developer trying Redwood for the first time, I want a guided demo that returns a meaningful assistant response from a pre-built persona so I can evaluate the product without writing code.
Acceptance criteria: demo returns streaming response in < 1s median, shows token estimate, shows expected cost band.

2) As a product manager evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs, I want a fidelity slider so I can directly observe differences in latency and cost between settings.
Acceptance criteria: slider triggers model variant switch or adjusts sampling + max tokens; UI updates token estimate & last-run latency.

3) As an engineer, I want the concierge to recommend fallback routes (cheaper variant or cached response) for common queries so I can see how routing would affect my workload.
Acceptance criteria: top-2 fallback suggestions displayed with cost delta and suggested latency improvement.

Edge stories / nice-to-have:
- Per-user memory switch that toggles short-term session KV caching for persona warm starts.
- Quick A/B toggle to test dedicated vs hosted policy (for internal demos only).

Design sketch / flow (rough):
- Step 0: welcome screen with 3 persona cards (Support Agent, Product Coach, Sales Briefing). Each card shows an example prompt and one-line expected output.
- Step 1: pick persona -> UI pre-populates sample prompt (editable). Shows fidelity slider and token/cost estimate panel.
- Step 2: run query -> streaming response panel + latency meter + toggle to view request/response JSON. Shows inline “use cheaper fallback” CTA if request exceeds threshold.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Reuse existing hosted-api endpoints; no new model onboarding needed for MVP.
- Prefill persona instructions as short system messages (<= 120 chars) to keep prefix small for cost control.
- Caching: store persona KV prefix in ephemeral session store; invalidate after 24h or when edited.
- Security: do not collect freeform user data for analytics by default — only sample hash of prompts for drift detection.

Metrics to track (initial):
- Conversion: % of users who submit >1 query after demo (goal: 30% within first week).
- Engagement: avg queries per demo session, median latency, tokens per session.
- Economics: median cost per demo session, distribution of fidelity slider choices.
- Signals for product: common freeform prompts (hashed), percent opting into session memory, fallback suggestion acceptance rate.

Experiment plan (30 day):
- Week 1: internal dogfood + SRE smoke test. Test streaming, prefilling, token estimates across regions.
- Week 2: soft launch to signups in US-only, capture telemetry, manual review for safety-eval hits.
- Week 3: expose to 25% of new signups, start A/B: default fidelity = econ vs default=qual.
- Week 4: analyze signals, iterate persona list and cost estimates.

Rollout & gating:
- Gate on SLOs: median completion latency < 1.2s, error rate < 1% on demo runs.
- Manual approval from Product + Security for public rollout (safety checks on sample prompts).

Open questions / risks (todo):
- UX: how opinionated should personas be? If too narrow, people won’t see their use-case; too broad and the demo is noisy.
- Cost clarity: how to surface cost without scaring devs? Inline estimate + clear banding? Percentile view?
- Caching semantics: privacy concerns if session memory persists across signups in shared demos. Need review by Security.
- Model variants: do we just swap full model family or tune sampling + max tokens? Engineering complexity differs.

Action items / next steps (notes-to-self):
- [ ] Build minimal React flow using existing SDK demo components (ask DevEx for component refs).
- [ ] Wire telemetry events (event names + schemas) — ping Analytics for schema review.
- [ ] Draft short copy for 3 personas (Maya to write samples).
- [ ] Safety review: shortlist prohibited prompt patterns and detection thresholds (Arjun to lead).
- [ ] Decide pricing-calculation UI (simple banded estimate for MVP).

Slack crumbs / links: see #product-concierge pinned messages for sample persona copy. Also check Confluence page "companion-concierge-overview" for earlier notes (ancient; ignore technical debt there).

Random brainstorming fragments (leave in for ideation):
- Could be a webhook mode: allow onboarding flow to return a signed demo token that customers can use in their first SDK calls to pre-populate persona.
- Tiny templating language: allow variable placeholders like {{user_name}} to surface in examples (but that increases prefix complexity).
- Offer a single-click export: create a snippet that sets up the persona + routing policy in the customer's project (for sticky onboarding).

Keep this messy; will refine into a longer PRD after we get telemetry from dogfood.

-- Kai
(quick note: pair with DevEx for component time estimate; ping SRE about streaming quotas)
